The Śrī Guhyasamāja Tantra. Oṃ, homage to the glorious Vajrasattva. The first chapter.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling within the secret bhagas of the Vajra Consorts, which are the hearts of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

(ṅ.O.ṣ. p. 58 thus: “The heart is gnosis; that itself is the Vajra-lady because its nature is indivisible and impartial; that itself is the *bhaga* because it shatters all afflictions (*kleśa*). [He] dwelt there with [retinues] inexpressible and beyond expression.”
[Accompanied] by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in all the Mount Sumerus of all Buddha-fields; namely:
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Samayavajra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Kāyavajra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vāgvajra, and the [Bodhisattva Mahāsattva] named Cittavajra.
by the bodhisattva mahāsattva; by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Samādhivajra;
by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Japavajra; by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Pṛthivīvajra; and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Abvajra.
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Tejovajra; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vāyuvajra; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Ākāśavajra;
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Rūpavajra; and by the Bodhisattva named Śabdavajra.
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Gandhavajra; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Rasavajra.
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sparśavajra,
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Dharmadhātuvajra—
headed by these [bodhisattvas], as numerous as the atoms in the Mount Sumerus of unspeakably unspeakable buddha-fields—
Thus it was proclaimed by the Tathāgatas— namely, by the Tathāgata named Akṣobhyavajra, by the Tathāgata named Vairocanavajra,
by the Tathāgata named Ratnaketuvajra, and by Amitavajra.
And by the Tathāgata named Amoghasiddhi, and by the Tathāgata named Amoghavajra— by such leading Tathāgatas as these, who fill the entire realm of space.
It was as follows: indeed, the entire realm of space appeared completely filled with all the Tathāgatas, like a sesame seed pod.
Then, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana—
Having entered the meditative absorption named *Sarvatathāgatamahārāganaya*,
he caused that array of all the Tathāgatas to enter into the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind. Then, those all the Tathāgatas [of the Blessed One...]

[End. For the purpose of pleasing the Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, they emanated their own forms as female forms; having emerged from the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, they came to abide within his heart. Therein—
Some remained in the form of Buddhalocanā, some in the form of Māmakī, some in the form of Pāṇḍaravāsinī, and some in the form of Samayatārā (pdf 26, p. 3).

There, some remained established with the aspect of the intrinsic nature of form, some with the aspect of the intrinsic nature of sound, some with the aspect of the intrinsic nature of taste, and some with the aspect of the intrinsic nature of touch.
Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya— [kh, g: vajra]— [remained].
He empowered the four-cornered, stainless Great Samaya Maṇḍala within the bhagas of the Vajra Ladies, who are the heart-vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas;
it was transparent, of that very nature, and possessed various forms on all sides.
The city of all the Tathāgatas is filled with clouds of Buddhas, blazing with a dense mass of sparks, and endowed with circles of pure light.
Then the Blessed One, the Lord of the Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, established himself in the center of the maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas. Then indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya,
the Tathāgata Ratnaketu, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, and the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi—
The Tathāgata Vairocana dwelt in the heart of the Tathāgata Bodhicittavajra.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bodhicittavajra, entered the samādhi called "the vajra that overcomes all Tathāgatas. And immediately upon his entering [that samādhi], this Lord of all Tathāgatas—then this...
The entire realm of space became established as the vajra-samaya of all Tathāgatas. Then, as many sentient beings as there were residing throughout the entire realm of space, they all—
by means of that empowerment of Vajrasattva— attained the bliss and mental well-being of all Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bodhicittavajra, entered the meditative absorption named the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas, and [uttered] this:

[He] empowered the form of the Great Knowledge Being (mahāvidyāpuruṣa), which is the empowerment of the mantras of all Tathāgatas. As soon as it was thus empowered, that very Blessed One, Vairocana-vajra Tathāgata, appeared in a three-faced form.
He was seen by all the Tathāgatas.
Then, all the Tathāgatas, headed by Akṣobhya, emerged from the heart of the Blessed One Bodhicittavajra [Vairocana] and uttered this inspired utterance:
With joy [he exclaimed]: "Oh, how marvelous is the arousal of the thought of enlightenment among all Buddhas!
This secret of all Tathāgatas is not to be revealed to those who are defiled. Thus it is said.

Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having again assembled in the great assembly, worshipped the Blessed One, the Vajra of Bodhicitta, with clouds of jewels of the reality of the samaya that pervades the worship and consecration of all Tathāgatas; and having prostrated, they spoke as follows:
"Speak, O Blessed One, the reality of the *Vajrasārasamuccaya*, the secret of all Tathāgatas, the *Samāja* born from the secret. Thus it is said.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bodhicittavajra, spoke thus to all those Tathāgatas: "Excellent, excellent, O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas! However—"
"This causes doubt even for all the Tathāgatas; how much more so for other Bodhisattvas?
Then the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas, were struck with wonder and filled with amazement toward the Blessed One, the dispeller of the doubts of all the Tathāgatas.

They questioned the Lord of all Tathāgatas: "O Blessed One, why is it that even though you are in this assembly of all Tathāgatas distinguished by such qualities, you do not venture to explain the secret of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas? Then the Blessed One...
Having performed the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas by means of the words "arising from the vajra-samaya of all the Tathāgatas" (p.
27, l. 5), for the purpose of causing all the Tathāgatas to experience joy in their faces.
"...for the sake of attaining the fruit of the knowledge and superknowledges of all Tathāgatas, it was thus proclaimed.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajra,
having understood the request of all the Tathāgatas, [entered] the samādhi named Jñānapradīpavajra.

Having entered [this state], he emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this supreme essence-heart-mantra of the entire family of Hatred: *Vajradhṛk*. Then, as soon as this was spoken, that very Blessed One became the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
Through the supreme states of union with the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of Akṣobhya, in the form of black, white, and red,
he caused [the deity] to sit upon the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, from the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called "Vajra Arising from the Samaya of All Tathāgatas" and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this supreme essence-heart of the delusion family: *jinajik*. As soon as this was spoken, that very Blessed One...
The embodiment of the secret essence of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, through the supreme states of union with the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of Vairocana—
manifesting in white, black, and red forms— sat down before the Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgataratnasambhavavajrendriya and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this supreme essence-heart of the Cintāmaṇi family: RATNADHṚK. Then, in this...
As soon as it was spoken, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas,
by means of the supreme states of union with the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Ratnaketu, [appeared] in the forms of yellow, white, and black, [as] the body, speech, and... of all Tathāgatas.
He caused him to sit down to the right of Cittavajra.
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Arising from the Great Passion of All Tathāgatas," and [uttered] this supreme essence-heart-mantra of the Vajra-Passion Family.

He emitted [it] from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind: *ĀROLIK*. Then, as soon as this was spoken, that very Blessed One—the Vidyā-puruṣa of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, the Great Lord of Vidyās, Lokeśvara—by means of the supreme state of union with the Great Mudrā, [performed...]
In the form of red, white, and black, he caused it to arise behind the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Unfailing Samaya of All Tathāgatas, and [uttered] this supreme essence-heart-mantra for summoning the family of the samaya:
From the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, he brought forth [the mantra]: *prajñādhṛk*.

Then, as soon as this was spoken, that very Blessed One, the Vidyā-puruṣa of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, [seated himself] upon the north of the Vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, through the union with the Great Mudrā of Amoghavajra.
"Hatred, delusion, and likewise passion, as well as the vow of the wish-fulfilling gem—these are indeed the five families that accomplish both desire and liberation. Thus it is said.

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called "The Commitment of Pleasing All Tathāgatas and Vajradharas," and from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, [he brought forth] this supreme queen of all Vajradharas.
He uttered: *dveṣarati*. Then, as soon as this had issued forth, that very Blessed One became the Knowledge-Man (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Assuming the form of a woman, he caused Dveṣarati to sit in the eastern corner of the mandala—preceding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas. (Note: Although some manuscripts read "southern corner" or "eastern corner," since Dveṣarati is the consort of Akṣobhya, she must be situated in the center of the maṇḍala circle.)
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra of Passion for All Tathāgatas and emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind this supreme queen of all Tathāgatas: Moharati.
Then, as soon as she had emerged,
that very Blessed One— the Vidyā-puruṣa of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas— assuming his own form, appeared in the eastern corner.

[Kh, g: 51 Dakṣiṇa] he caused her to sit down. Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra of Delighting in the Jewel of All Tathāgatas, and from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, he brought forth this foremost queen who holds all forms of envy: Īrṣyārati.

Then, as soon as she had emerged, that very Blessed One—the Vidyā-puruṣa of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas—assuming a female form, caused her to sit in the southern corner. [The diagram (Fig. 1) will clearly show that a long portion (of which a...]
[The conjectural restoration provided here must have been omitted by the copyists.

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Passion-Holder of All Tathāgatas, and from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, [he brought forth] this foremost queen who holds all passions.
He brought forth [the mantra] *rāgarati*. Then, as soon as this had issued forth, that very Blessed One—
the Vidyā-puruṣa of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas— assumed a female form and sat down in the western corner.

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Non-deception of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas, and from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, he brought forth this supreme queen who upholds the wisdom of all Tathāgatas:
Vajrarati. As soon as she had emerged, that very Blessed One...
The Knowledge-Person (vidyāpuruṣa) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, having assumed the form of a woman, sat down in the northern corner.
[k, g: add "together with the consorts of the supreme queens of all Tathāgatas"]. Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi of Mahāvairocana-vajra and [uttered] this:

He emitted from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the great wrathful deity named Sarvatathāgatamaṇḍalādhiṣṭhāna (The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas), namely Yamāntakṛt. Then, as soon as he had issued forth— (pdf 29, p. 9)
That very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, sat at the eastern gate in the form of one who terrifies all Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One [entered] the samādhi called the Vajra of the Perfect Awakening of All Tathāgatas.
Having entered this great wrathful deity named "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas," he caused it to issue forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.

Prajñāntakṛt. Then, as soon as he had emerged, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, sat at the southern gate in the form of the Vajra-Samaya-Terrorizer.

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatadharmavaśaṅkarī (the One Who Brings All Tathāgatas Under the Power of Dharma) and, from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind, emitted this great wrathful deity named Sarvatathāgatarāgadharamaṇḍalādhiṣṭhāna (the Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Passion of All Tathāgatas), namely Padmāntakṛt (the Destroyer of Lotuses).
Then, as soon as he had emerged, that very Blessed One, the Knowledge-Person (*vidyāpuruṣa*) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas,
sat down at the western gate in the form of the speech of all Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) called the Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas, and this—

He brought forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the great wrathful deity named Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittamaṇḍalādhiṣṭhāna, the Destroyer of Obstacles (Vighnāntakṛt). Then, as soon as he had issued forth,
that very Blessed One became the Knowledge-Person (vidyāpuruṣa) of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
In the form of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, he caused them to sit at the northern gate.
These are the beings of the samaya of the maṇḍala for conversing with the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
Thus, from the *Śrī-sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittarahasyātirahasya-guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras.
This respect has been secured in all places, and no variant or incomplete readings have been noted.
Chapter One: The First Section on the Empowerment of the Samādhi-maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas.

The Second Chapter. Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having performed worship to the Blessed Lord, the Sovereign of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, prostrated themselves and spoke as follows:
Having performed [this], O Blessed One, speak the essence, the supreme body, speech, and mind—
the secret of all Tathāgatas, the unsurpassed bodhicitta.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajra, having understood the request of all the Tathāgatas and having known with his own mind the mental reflection of all the Bodhisattvas, spoke thus to the Bodhisattvas:
"May you, sirs, generate the mind in the form of the body, the body in the form of the mind, and the mind through the utterance of speech.
Then those great bodhisattvas, having joined them together in the form of the space-like body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas...
They uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, by means of the application of non-arising, this arising of Samantabhadra, the Vajra of Body, Speech, and Mind, is proclaimed."
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajra, entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Method for the Perfect Enlightenment of All Tathāgatas, and uttered this bodhicitta:
In the absence [of an object], there is no cultivation; cultivation is not truly cultivation.
Thus, existence would not be existence, and cultivation is not perceived.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajra.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocanavajra, [entered] the samādhi named Sarvatathāgatābhisamayavajra.

Having entered into meditative absorption, he uttered this thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*): "Free from all entities, devoid of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, and abandoned by the grasped and the grasper; through the equality of the selflessness of phenomena, one's own mind is primordially unarisen, the very nature of emptiness. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Vairocanavajra Tathāgata.
Then the Blessed One Akṣobhyavajra Tathāgata entered the samādhi called "The Indestructible Vajra of All Tathāgatas" and uttered this thought of awakening:
These entities are unarisen; they are neither phenomena nor the nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
Like space, this selflessness is the firm method of awakening.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhyavajra.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnaketuvajra, entered the samādhi called the Vajra of Selflessness of All Tathāgatas and uttered this bodhicitta:
All phenomena are non-existent; they are devoid of the characteristics of phenomena. Arising from the selflessness of phenomena—this is the firm method of awakening.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnaketuvajra.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyurvajra, [entered] the samādhi named Sarvatathāgatajñānārciḥpradīpavajra.
Having entered [meditative absorption], he uttered this thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*):
"When phenomena have not arisen, there is neither existence nor cultivation."
The intended meaning is that it is proclaimed through its association with the term "space."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyurvajra.
(pdf 31, p.
13) Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhivajra, [spoke] the [samādhi] named Sarvatathāgatābhibhavanavajra.
Having entered into meditative absorption, he uttered this thought of awakening:
"All phenomena are luminous by nature, utterly pure, and equal to space."
There is no awakening, nor is there realization; this is the firm method of awakening for beings.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhivajra.
Then indeed, the great Bodhisattvas headed by Maitreya [regarding] the syllable of the secret reality of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas...
Attaining wonder and attaining amazement, they uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oho, the Buddha! Oho, the Dharma! Oho, the teaching of the Saṅgha!"
O you whose purpose is the pure reality, whose purpose is purity, the awakened mind—homage be to you!
Born from the selflessness of phenomena, fulfilling the enlightenment of the Buddhas,
non-conceptual and without support— homage be to you, O Bodhicitta!
Samantabhadra, who acts for the benefit of sentient beings, you who set in motion the thought of awakening; O Great Vajra of the conduct of awakening, homage be to you, the thought of awakening!
The mind of the Tathāgatas is pure; you who hold the vajras of body, speech, and mind, the bestower of the awakening of the Buddhas—O Bodhicitta, homage be to you!

Thus ends the second chapter, the Chapter on Bodhicitta, in the *Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, which is the most secret of secrets regarding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
The third chapter. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajra of Body, Speech, and Mind,
entered the meditative absorption named *Vajra Array of Clouds Pervading All Tathāgatas* [and said this].
He fully proclaimed the chapter on meditative absorption named "Vajra Array, Vajra Array": "Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the wisdom of emptiness.
One should visualize the maṇḍala of the Buddhas situated in the center of the space-element."
A great array of clouds of light rays, with a radiance equal to the flames of a Buddha.
It is completely surrounded by a circle of five-colored rays,
filled with the five qualities of sensual pleasure, and adorned with the five types of offerings.
Having meditated in brief, one should visualize the syllable *kha* in the center of the image.
One should meditate upon the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of Vairocana, characterized by body, speech, and mind,
or else one should visualize the seal of the Vajra of Body, Speech, and Mind.
The supreme mudrā of Akṣobhya through the application of the two accumulations;
the great mudrā of Ratnakeśin and the light-making [mudrā] of Amitāyus.
One should meditate upon the great mudrā of Amoghasiddhi within the Buddha-maṇḍala,
appearing with the luster of sapphire and possessing the vajras of body, speech, and mind.
Holding a vajra in his hand, possessing great radiance, and terrifying with his formidable and fierce appearance;
having the luster of crystal and the moon, and adorned with a crown of matted locks.
Holding a wheel in his hand, with great radiance, adorned with various ornaments,
possessing the luster of Jāmbūnada gold, and filled with clouds of Buddhas.
One should visualize in his hand the great nine-pronged vajra, having the luster of emerald and adorned with vajra-flames. (pdf 32, p. 15)
Having visualized him holding a jewel in his hand— a mass of flames and clouds on all sides—
having the appearance of the luster of a ruby, and adorned with a crown of matted locks.
One should meditate upon Rāgavajrin, who holds a lotus in his hand, possesses great radiance,
has a form consisting of the light of five rays, and is the embodiment of Amoghavajrin.
One should visualize the gentle Buddha-maṇḍala holding a sword in its hand.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajra of Body, Speech, and Mind, entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Essential Nature of the Dharmadhātu and uttered this mantra for the empowerment of body, speech, and mind: OṂ.
I am of the nature of the vajra of the dharmadhātu.
One should always meditate, through yoga and with effort, upon a great five-colored jewel the size of a mustard seed at the tip of the nose.
One should expand the stable jewel, but one should never expand the unstable;
one should expand it with excellent clouds possessing a radiance equal to vajra-flames.
One whose nature is emanation should cause emanations to spread forth by means of great clouds of wheels and vajras, great clouds of lotus-buds and supreme weapons, and great clouds of bodhisattvas.
One should draw a vajra-maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
one should meditate upon a wheel-maṇḍala situated in the midst of a translucent maṇḍala.
One should meditate on that which resembles a lotus mandala through the meditations on the lotus;
one intent on the jewel should meditate on that which resembles a jewel mandala.
One should draw that which is born from the yoga-maṇḍala in the vicinity of space;
these indeed are the most excellent Buddhas through the meditations on body, speech, and mind.
Born from the vajra-maṇḍala, they have attained the form of omniscience.

Thus ends the third chapter on meditative absorption, titled “The Vajra Array,” from the *Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets regarding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
The Fourth Chapter. Then the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas, having again assembled in a gathering, [addressed] the Blessed One,
the Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, with this...
They made this request with the King of Praises:
"Teach the supreme maṇḍala, which is peaceful and belongs to all Tathāgatas, the abode of all Tathāgatas, and the foremost selflessness of all phenomena."
Perfectly endowed with all marks and yet devoid of all marks,
speak of the supreme maṇḍala, the foremost body of Samantabhadra.
Proclaim the supreme maṇḍala, born from the foremost of peaceful phenomena, which purifies the conduct of gnosis, and is the most excellent speech of Samantabhadra.
The great mind of all sentient beings is pure and naturally stainless; it is the supreme Samantabhadra-citta, the most excellent mandala of sound.
Then Vajradhara, the Teacher, who is the three worlds and the triple realm,
the supreme and foremost Vajra of the three worlds, the instructor of the highest in the three worlds.
The delightful mandala, the abode of all Tathāgatas, shines forth;
the mind of all Tathāgatas is the mandala, having the form of a mandala.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of the mind,
which resembles the vajra of the mind— the maṇḍala of body, speech, and mind.
The wise one should trace out the lines with a new, perfectly pure, well-measured, and beautiful thread, by means of the meditations on body, speech, and mind.
One should construct the supreme *cittamaṇḍala* measuring twelve cubits;
one should fashion it as square, with four doors and four corners. (pdf 34, p. 18)
Within that, one should draw a circular wheel;
then, one should perform the placement of the mudrās according to the ritual procedure prescribed by rule.
In its center, one should draw a five-pronged vajra with the luster of sapphire, possessing great flames and terrifying even fear itself.
To the east is the great wheel, adorned with vajra-flames;
to the south is the great jewel, agitated by a dense mass of sparks.
To the west, one should draw the Great Lotus, with a luster equal to a ruby;
to the north, the Great Sword, blazing and enveloped in a mass of flaming rays.
In the eastern corner, one should draw the Eye, with a luster equal to the midst of clouds;
then, to the south, the Vajra born from the family of Māmakī.
To the west, one should draw a lotus with its stalk and fully blossomed face;
to the north, one should fashion an utpala flower, beautiful like a dark blue cloud.
One should draw a mallet, brilliantly radiant with flames, at the eastern gate;
to the south, one should draw a staff, brilliantly radiant with vajra-flames and so forth.
To the west, one should draw a lotus that radiates the light of a flaming sword;
to the north, one should draw a vajra belonging to Vajrakuṇḍalī, the wielder of the vajra.
Having clearly realized the supreme mandala of the mind known as consciousness,
one should diligently perform worship through the offerings of body, speech, and mind.
Having obtained a sixteen-year-old woman of radiant beauty,
and having covered her with perfumes and flowers, one should desire her in the midst of that.
And having donned that wisdom-girdle of mine,
the wise one should create the gentle state of Buddhahood, adorned by the realm of space.
One should offer feces, urine, semen, blood, and so forth to the deities;
in this way, the perfectly awakened Buddhas and the high-minded Bodhisattvas are satisfied.

Thus ends the fourth chapter, the Chapter on the Secret Maṇḍala of Body, Speech, and Mind, in the *Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the Most Secret of Secrets of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.
The Fifth Chapter.
Then the Blessed One, the Holder of the Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, the King, the Foremost of All, the Lord of the World;
For the sake of the Dharma, he speaks of the supreme practice of the Dharma, which is characterized by conduct.
One should accomplish the supreme siddhi in this unsurpassed, foremost vehicle, which arises from the non-conceptual object and is the great lineage of passion and hatred [and delusion].
Even those such as Caṇḍālas and bamboo-workers, who contemplate wealth for the purpose of killing,
attain accomplishment in this supreme vehicle, the Mahāyāna.
Even those who have committed the great sins, such as the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*),
attain accomplishment in this Buddha-vehicle, this great ocean of the Mahāyāna.
Those intent on reviling their preceptor do not succeed in the practice;
nor do those beings who take life and who delight in false speech.
Those who are constantly intent on the wealth of others, those who are ever devoted to sensual pleasures,
and those whose purpose is the consumption of feces and urine— they are indeed fit for the practice of sādhana.
The practitioner who desires his mother, sister, or daughter shall attain vast accomplishment, the supreme reality of the Mahāyāna among all phenomena.
Even while desiring the mother of the all-pervading Buddha, he is not defiled;
for that wise one who is free from conceptual construction, Buddhahood is accomplished.
(From *pdf* 35, p.

21) Then indeed, the great bodhisattvas headed by Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhin, having attained a state of wonder and having attained a state of amazement, [asked]: "What is this, O Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas?"

In the midst of the assembly circles of all the Tathāgatas, he uttered words that were ill-spoken. Then, all those Tathāgatas [addressed] the great Bodhisattvas, beginning with Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhin...
Having heard these words of wonder concerning Great Enlightenment, they spoke thus to those bodhisattvas:
"Enough, sons of good family; do not speak in this way.
This is the pure nature of reality (dharmatā) of the Buddhas, who possess knowledge of the essence."
This very path of the conduct of awakening (*bodhicaryāpada*), born from the meaning of the essential Dharma, is for the sake of sentient beings.
Then, indeed, those bodhisattvas— equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many buddha-fields— became afraid, terrified, and fainted.

Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, seeing those Bodhisattvas fallen into a swoon, spoke thus to the Blessed Lord, the Sovereign of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas: "Blessed One, please rouse these Great Bodhisattvas!"
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajra, entered the meditative absorption named Ākāśasamatādvayavajra. Immediately upon the Blessed One,
the Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, having entered that state, by means of his radiance...

As soon as they were touched, those bodhisattvas became established in their respective seats. Then all those Tathāgatas, having attained a state of wonder and amazement, overflowing with joy, spoke thus:
They made a proclamation of the Dharma regarding all phenomena:
"O Dharma! O Dharma! O source of the meaning of the Dharma! (pdf 36, p. 22)
Homage, homage to Vajrarāja, whose nature is the purity of phenomena and the selflessness of objects.
Purified in body, speech, and mind, abiding in equality with space,
changeless and without appearance— homage, homage to the Vajra Body!
Homage, homage to the supreme mind of the Tathāgatas, which abides on the path of the three times; it is the great space that has become the element, the meaning of space—homage, homage!
Born from the body of space, the activator of speech that is space,
the supreme dharma of the mind that is space— homage be to you, the stage of conduct!

Thus ends the fifth chapter, the foremost section on universal conduct, in the *Śrī-guhyasamāja*, the great king of secret tantras, the most secret of secrets regarding the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
The Sixth Chapter. Then indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhyavajra entered the meditative absorption named the Secret Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, and this—
He uttered the mantra of the mental empowerment:
|| Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-mind of all Tathāgatas. ||
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocanavajra, entered the samādhi called Virajapadavajra and uttered this mantra for the empowerment of the body:
|| Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-body of all Tathāgatas. ||
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyurvajra, entered the samādhi called "The Non-dual Vajra of the Equality of All Tathāgatas" and uttered this mantra for the empowerment of speech:
OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAVĀGVAJRASVABHĀVĀTMAKO 'HAM.
One should accomplish the pure, Tathāgata-like triple-vajra state, which is the manifestation of the stages,
by means of these supreme mantras characterized by the marks of mantra.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnaketuvajra, entered the samādhi called Jñānapradīpavajra and uttered this mantra of passion:
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the passion of all Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhivajra, having entered the meditative absorption named Amoghavajra, uttered this mantra of worship:
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of worship of all the Tathāgatas.

One should always worship the Buddhas with the five strands of sensual pleasure according to the prescribed ritual, by means of their very qualities. (pdf 37, p. 24) [k: by means of their very quality; g: by means of the ritual]
Through the fivefold offerings of worship, one shall swiftly attain Buddhahood.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara, the Lord of the Vajras of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas. Then the Blessed One, Vajradhara, the Lord of the Vajras of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas,
proclaimed this secret mantra of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, I am of the very nature of the vajra body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas.
Impelled by body, speech, and mind through the contemplation of mantra,
one should accomplish the supreme siddhi, which is dear to those whose minds are satisfied.
Through the selflessness of mental concentration and the dissolution of speech and body,
they accomplish the union that is the abode of equality with space.
Through the contemplation of body, speech, and mind, no intrinsic nature is perceived;
by means of the application of the mantra-form,
one meditates upon the awakening-mind (bodhicitta).
Having briefly reflected upon this characteristic of body, speech, and mind as it is perceived,
one should cultivate the meditative absorption (samādhi) fashioned by mantra, which is conjoined with the ritual procedure.
Then the glorious Vajradhara, accompanied by all the Tathāgatas,
the omniscient one who is foremost among all Buddhas, spoke this supreme meditation:
One should meditate on a moon-maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
having visualized the image of the Buddha, one should commence the subtle yoga.
(From PDF 37, p.
25) One should contemplate a mustard seed at the tip of the nose; within that mustard seed is the world with its moving and unmoving beings.
One should meditate upon this delightful secret, fashioned by gnosis, which bestows knowledge.
One should visualize a sun-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
having clearly manifested the form of the Buddha, one should place the seed-syllable upon it.
HŪṂ!
One should meditate on the maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
one should visualize the union of Locanā’s form with the vajra and lotus.
One should meditate on a jewel maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
with diligence, one should visualize the primordial yoga (ādiyoga) upon it.
One should meditate on a lotus maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
one should meditate on Rāgavajrin, who is perfectly joined in the form of a lotus and has the luster of a ruby. One should meditate on a circle of rays situated in the midst of the space-element.
One should emit the peaceful state of the Buddha, especially its retinue.
One should diligently visualize at the tip of the nose a five-pronged [vajra] shaped like the petal of a blue lotus, specifically the size of a barley grain.
One intent on awakening should clearly visualize this eight-petaled lotus with its filaments, the size of a chickpea husk, at the tip of the nose.
One should specifically cultivate the meditation on the wheel and the other [symbols] therein;
thus one will attain the delightful state of awakening, the abode of the qualities of mantra-perfection.
Therein, one should briefly emanate that which is established in the awakening of the Buddhas;
one should cause the word of Dharma to issue forth, characterized by body, speech, and mind.
(From PDF 38, p.
26) Then the glorious Vajradhara, the teacher of the meaning of all reality,
who has arisen from the foremost of all practices, spoke this supreme secret:
For six months, the wise one, endowed with form, sound, and taste, should practice meditation;
having performed the great worship of the secret reality, he should contemplate it.
One who desires the fruit of accomplishment should perform the function of consuming feces and urine;
thus, that unsurpassed reality—the stainless *bodhicitta*—is accomplished.
For the purpose of performing activities such as eating meat, one should prepare "great flesh" (mahāmāṃsa);
thus the secret of body, speech, and mind is accomplished among all attainments.
One should eat the flesh of elephants, the flesh of horses, and likewise the flesh of dogs for the purpose of taking food; one should not consume anything else.
He becomes beloved of the Buddhas and of the wise Bodhisattvas;
indeed, by means of this very yoga, he shall swiftly attain Buddhahood.
He shall become a lord over the world of the desire realm, performing the tasks of others;
he will be radiant, powerful, preeminent, beautiful, and pleasing to behold.
One should honor this in the world, being impelled by the very vision;
for this is the secret of all Buddhas, the supreme enlightenment,
the reality of the secret mantra characterized by body, speech, and mind.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, the section on the Empowerment of Body, Speech, and Mind, in the *Guhyasamāja*, the King of Great Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets concerning the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
The Seventh Chapter.
Then the Blessed One, the Lord of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, [spoke] on the supreme awakening through the practice of mantras as the Great Compendium—
While enjoying all objects of desire as one wishes,
by means of this very yoga, one shall indeed swiftly attain Buddhahood.
While enjoying all objects of desire as one pleases,
one should worship by means of the yoga with one's own presiding deity and with the supreme limbs (or supreme portions, or offerings).
One who practices with difficult and intense restraints does not achieve success;
however, by enjoying all objects of desire, one achieves success quickly.
One who subsists on alms should not perform recitation, nor should he be devoted to begging;
one whose limbs are not impaired by the mantras of recitation may enjoy all objects of desire.
Having attained the well-being of body, speech, and mind, one attains enlightenment;
otherwise, one certainly undergoes untimely death and is cooked in hell.
Buddhas and bodhisattvas who practice the supreme conduct of mantra have attained the most excellent seat of Dharma through the enjoyment of all desired objects.
One who seeks knowledge should always enjoy the five objects of desire;
he should satisfy the Bodhisattvas and delight them with the hero of passion.
Having understood form as threefold, one who is devoted to worship should perform worship;
he is thus the Blessed One, the wise Buddha, the Lord Vairocana.
(From PDF 39, p.
28) Having understood sound to be of three kinds, one should offer it to the deities.
Such is the Blessed One, the Buddha, the Lord who is a mine of the jewels of the Buddhas.
Having recognized the threefold scent, one should offer it to the Buddha and the others;
he is thus the Blessed Buddha, the Lord who upholds the Dharma of passion.
Having understood the threefold flavor, one should offer it to the deities;
he is indeed the Blessed One, the Buddha, who possesses the unfailing vajra.
Having known the threefold touch,
one should offer it to one's own family;
he is thus the Blessed One, the Vajrin, who has attained the form of Akṣobhya.
One should always apply forms, sounds, tastes, and so forth to the mind;
this is the compendium of the secret essence of all Buddhas.
The practitioner of mantra should always meditate upon the deity through touch, sound, and so forth;
or else, he should meditate there by means of discerning the various divisions of the *kula*.
The cultivation of mindfulness through the recollection of the Buddha and the application of mindfulness to the Saṅgha;
the cultivation of the cultivation of the recollection of the vajras of body, speech, and mind.

Through the yoga of recollecting the family, one should cultivate the recollection of the wrathful deity; by means of the yoga of recollecting the commitment (*samaya*), one who cultivates thus shall attain awakening.
Having obtained such a woman, endowed with beauty and radiant luster, who possesses that specific power,
one should secretly begin the worship while maintaining the recollection of the stages of empowerment.
One should visualize either Locanā, who is the great radiance of the Tathāgata, or [Bodhi];
through the union of the two organs,
one shall attain the accomplishment of Buddhahood.
One should conceptualize the syllables *hūṃ*, *oṃ*, and *paṃ*;
one should meditate upon a vajra-lotus pervaded by five-colored rays of light.

One who desires awakening should meditate upon that delightful [goddess], blazing like a ray of light from a vajra; one who longs for enlightenment should practice the yoga of the recollection of the Buddhas and so forth.
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the Buddha performed?
One should visualize the form of the Buddha through the union of the two organs;
the wise one should radiate clouds of Buddhas from the openings of the pores of his skin.
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the Dharma performed?
Through the union of the two organs, one should visualize Vajradharma;
the wise one should radiate clouds of Dharma from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin.
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the Vajra performed?
Through the union of the two organs, one should visualize Vajrasattva;
the wise one should emanate clouds of vajras from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin.
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the family (*kulānusmṛti*) performed?
Through the union of the two organs, one should visualize the form of the Buddha;
the wise one should emanate clouds of the [Buddha] families from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin.
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of wrath performed?
Through the union of the two organs, one should visualize the Lord of Wrath;
the wise practitioner should emanate clouds of wrath from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin.
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the pledge (samayānusmṛti) performed?
By means of the application of the two organs— the union of one's own vajra with the lotus—
one should worship the Buddhas and the Vajrasattvas with the drops of one's own semen.
(From *pdf* 40, p.
30) In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the mandala performed?
By means of the union of the two organs, the wise one [should contemplate] his own semen.
The yogin should always extract from the mandalas those who have the form of mandalas.
In that regard, how is the cultivation of mindfulness of the body performed?
One should think: "Just as the bodies of all Buddhas are fully endowed with the five aggregates, may my own body likewise become firmly established in the nature of the Buddha-body."
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of speech performed?
"May my speech also become like that of Vajradharma, endowed with the perfection of logical reasoning, and equal to the Holder of the Dharma."
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the mind performed?
"Whatever is the mind of the wise Guhyakendra Samantabhadra,
may my mind also be like that, equal to the Holder of the Vajra."
In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of sentient beings [practiced]?
Whatever mind belongs to all sentient beings, characterized by body, speech, and mind,
such a mind is also mine— pervading like space.

In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the body, speech, and mind of all mantra-forms? "May my body become like the body of the Mantra-Vajra; may my speech likewise bring about the visualization of the body; and may my mind also become like that of the Mantra-holder, eternally so."

In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the pledge (*samayānusmṛti*) performed? For one who desires the fruit according to the rule of the procedure for the lord of the syllables of the pledge, one should honor the Tathāgata array; thus one will most certainly attain accomplishment.
(From *pdf* 40, p.
31) In that regard, how is the cultivation of the recollection of the commitment (*samaya*) of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) performed?
All [phenomena] are naturally luminous, unarisen, and without support.
There is no awakening, no clear realization, no end, and no arising.
In that regard, what is the cultivation of the recollection of non-arising?
Everything is luminous by nature, signless, and without syllables;
it is neither dual nor non-dual, peaceful, like space, and utterly pure.
In that regard, what is the cultivation of mindfulness through the worship of the family of hatred?
Having obtained a woman of twelve years who is steady-minded,
one should worship her with one's own semen according to the specific divisions of the family yoga.
By this, one shall attain in this very life the body of the Tathāgata and the mind of Vajradhara, as well as the speech of the supreme Holder of Dharma.

Those who are considered low-born, as well as others, attain accomplishment through the recitation of that [mantra] by means of the meditations on the indivisibility of the three vajras, once the body, speech, and mind have been perfected.

Thus ends the seventh chapter, the Chapter on Mantra Practice, in the *Guhyasamāja*, the Great King of Secret Tantras, the most secret of secrets concerning the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
The Eighth Chapter. Then the Blessed One Ratnaketu, the Tathāgata, addressed the Blessed One, the Sovereign Lord of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas,
the Supreme Lord, the Great Vajradhara, with this:

With this king of hymns, he made this request: "O Vajrasattva, purifier of the space-like conduct of the Mahāyāna, Samantabhadra, supreme among offerings, O best of Jinas, teach the foremost of offerings!"
O Vajra of passion, hatred, and delusion, instructor of the Vajrayāna; O supreme one, like the element of space, O abode of the Jinas, accept this offering of sound!
O Buddha, leader of the path to liberation, who establishes the way of the three vehicles, whose self is pure through auspiciousness, O Supreme among Men, accept this worship!
O Bodhicitta, wide-eyed one, turner of the wheel of Dharma,
pure in body, speech, and mind— homage be to you, Vajrayāna!
Then the King Vajradhara, the great syllable of all space,
the purpose of all consecrations, the Lord of all, who holds the vajra-jewel.
He proclaims the supreme worship of the Tathāgatas, which is established in the indivisibility of the three vajras,
which possesses the excellence of body, speech, and mind, and which arises from the Victors.
Having obtained a large-eyed maiden adorned with beauty and youth,
one should arrange twenty-five [units] in her secret place, extending even across [her body].
In a clean, secluded area of the earth, which is a peaceful and auspicious abode for the Son of the Conqueror,
one should always perform the sprinkling of pure water and the like, or the anointing with unguents, for the sake of worshipping the Conqueror.

The knower of the ritual procedure should place [the mantras] from the middle of the chest up to the top of the crown, and also within the space between the eyebrows (or, according to manuscript *kh*, within the feet).
One should perform the placement of the five families in the navel, the heart, and the secret place of the sons of the Victors.
One should meditate on the ocean of gnosis situated in the midst of the space-element; furthermore,
the wise one should meditate on himself within the moon, again in the heart, according to the rule.
And if he who holds the peaceful vajra should desire to perform the withdrawal,
he should [visualize] that stūpa made of the four jewels, adorned with blazing rays of light.
Having established the woman as the ocean of gnosis, the wise one should contemplate her as the abode;
from the pores of her own body, he should emanate clouds of offerings.
Having understood the fivefold lotus and the blue water-lily, the wise one who knows the ritual,
having prepared the three types of birth-substances, should offer them to the deities.
Having meditated upon the flower of the *karṇikāra*, as well as the *mallikā* and *yūthikā*,
and the flower of the *karavīra*, one should perform the worship.
One who is skilled in constant practice should visualize the wheel-maṇḍala with an extent of one hundred yojanas, and should likewise arrange the [deities of the] families.
The wise one should visualize a lotus, a vajra, a sword,
and an utpala flower within a most beautiful square area extending for ten million yojanas.
The wise one should meditate upon a shrine made of the four jewels, transparent and naturally pure, as a fly-whisk for the purpose of honoring the Kulas.
One should begin with the pure Yādavī using the five strands of sensual pleasure;
desiring awakening, one should constantly worship her with jewels, garments, and other offerings.
(As stated in *pdf* 42, p. 34:
One should always satisfy the deity with the five supreme offerings (*pañcopahāra-pūjā*).
[One should offer] a maiden who brings forth jewels, most excellent, and adorned with various gems and ornaments.
For the sake of attaining accomplishment for all the Buddhas, the intense practitioners,
being wise, should offer this [mandala] made complete with the seven precious gems.
Desiring the accomplishment of the ocean of generosity, the wise one should daily offer it while assuming the mudrā of the Lord of Rays (the Sun) from the midst of the Buddha-maṇḍala.
One should bestow the union of touch with a mind of passion toward the Buddhas;
one should meditate upon the Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element.
Those who worship an image of the Tathāgata with the prescribed rites— using even feces and urine—
swiftly attain a woman who is fortunate, beautiful of face, and most excellent.
Having meditated upon the stage of empowerment, one should perform the worship of reality;
the wide-eyed one of firm intellect should consume the secret semen.
This is the worship of the body, speech, and mind of all mantras;
it is declared to be the secret that brings about the accomplishment of mantra for those possessing the vajra of gnosis.
Thus ends the eighth chapter, the Chapter on the Commitment of Mind, in the *Guhyasamāja*, the King of Great Secret Tantras, the Ultimate Secret of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas.
The Ninth Chapter. Now, King Vajradhara, the great syllable of all space,
the foremost in all consecrations and conduct, the omniscient Supreme Lord.
The union of body, speech, and mind is the mandala of the indivisible three vajras;
it proclaims the supreme, most delightful secret of those possessing the wisdom of the Buddhas.
One should visualize the maṇḍala of the Buddhas situated in the midst of the space-element;
having visualized Akṣobhyavajra, one should then visualize a vajra in one's hand.
Having meditated there upon the sovereign power of the Buddha, which is filled with a dense mass of sparks, illuminated by splendor, and suffused with five rays of light;
One should pulverize it with a vajra.
One should meditate upon the supreme dhyāna that brings about the accomplishment of the mind, in which the union of body, speech, and mind is pulverized by the eight vajras.
By means of this secret vajra, one should strike down all sentient beings—
even those who are the heart-born sons of the Victors in the Buddha-fields of this very vajra.

The union with the family of hatred should be known as the source of all families; having attained the family of hatred, one should be known as the ocean of all families, the exaltation of all families.
Then King Vajradhara, the accomplisher of wisdom and liberation,
pure by nature and untainted, set forth the conduct of awakening.
He speaks the reality of the pledge (*samaya*), which accomplishes the awakening of the Buddhas;
one should meditate upon the maṇḍala situated in the midst of the realm of space.
Having visualized Vairocana, one should visualize all the Buddhas;
by means of the application of all jewels, one should fashion the vajra-image.
One should visualize the seizing of all substances by means of the triple vajra;
they become like wish-fulfilling jewels, filled with an ocean of substances.
The preeminent sages become the legitimate sons of all Buddhas;
the reality equal to the family of delusion (mohakula) is to be known by those born from all families.
Then King Vajradhara, the accomplisher of passion and delusion, pure and without support in its secret nature, proclaimed the mandala.
One should visualize a lotus maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
having emanated Amitābha [from the seed-syllable *yūṃ*], one should fill everything with Buddhas.
One should visualize there the union with the form of a woman for all [beings] through the yoga of the four commitments; this is the supreme Vajra Way.
By means of the application of the two organs, one should enjoy them all;
this is the meditation on the non-differentiation of the three bodies of all Buddhas.
The practitioner of mantra should meditate upon the union of the passion family (rāgakula).
Then King Vajradhara, the accomplisher of the meaning of the vajra-mantras,
who is selfless and born of primordial wisdom, spoke these words:
One should visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the midst of the space-element;
having manifested Vajrāmogha, one should then visualize all the Buddhas.
One should visualize all forms through the vajra-word of false speech;
one should deceive all the Victors as well as all the abodes of the Victors.
(From PDF 43, p.
37) This, the space of speech of all Buddhas, is utterly pure;
it is declared to be the secret of those possessed of wisdom and intelligence, which brings about the accomplishment of mantra.
The family of the summoning of the pledge (samaya) should be impelled according to reality.
Then King Vajradhara, the leader of the Vajra of Accomplishment and the bearer of the indivisible triple-vajra, spoke these words:
Situated in the midst of the space-element, one should visualize the pledge-maṇḍala;
having manifested Ratnaketu, one should pervade this with all his forms.
"One may attain gnosis even by practicing harsh speech and the like," so said the Blessed One, the Vajra-Array of All Tathāgatas.
Then indeed, those great bodhisattvas, headed by Sarvatathāgatasamayavajraketu, being struck with wonder and filled with amazement,
uttered this sound of the vajra-voice:
"O Bodhisattva, how is it that the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, [has manifested] those who are distinct from the three realms?"

[Having performed the protection of the manifestation,] amidst the assemblies of all Tathāgatas and all Bodhisattvas, he spoke the vajra-word of the marvelous meaning of the speech, which transcends all world-systems.

Having meditated by means of the application of the tongue-vajra, one becomes equal to the speech-vajra;
having performed the supreme worship of the three secret samayas, one should manifest that worship.
"This is the ultimate essence of all accomplishments, the *Guhyasamuccaya*," so said the Blessed One, the Great Secret Samaya.
"By means of the foremost samaya of human flesh, one should accomplish the supreme Triple Vajra."
By means of the yoga of the excrement, urine, and the *samaya*, one becomes a powerful Lord of the Vidyādharas.
By means of the flesh of the elephant-samaya, one attains the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*);
by means of the flesh of the horse-samaya, one becomes a lord of invisibility (*antardhāna*).
(From *pdf* 53, p. 56):
By means of the dog-samaya-meat, all accomplishments (*siddhi*) are brought about;
by means of the cow-samaya at the forefront, the supreme vajra-attraction is achieved.
If all types of meat are unavailable, one should meditate upon and conceptualize them as sentient beings;
by means of this vajra-yoga, one is empowered by all the Buddhas.
Endowed with the excellence of all aspects, possessing the vajras of body, speech, and mind;
he has the wisdom-commitment (jñānasamaya) in his heart and bears the supreme vajra upon his crown.
This supreme method of the samaya, which delights all Buddhas, must be performed by one at the forefront of the samaya; it is the highest means for accomplishing all siddhis.
The samādhi called "Consuming the Vajra of All Samaya-Knowledge."
Having meditated on the Vajra-holder HŪṂ at the tip of the tongue— the tip of which is the samaya-vajra—
one shall attain the state of Vajrasattva through the application of the five nectars.
This is the commitment of the syllables ĀḤ and OṂ, the supreme Vajra method;
indeed, by means of this yoga, one becomes equal to Vajrasattva.
The Samādhi called the Garland of the Nectar of the Vajra of the Pledge.
For the sake of accomplishing the samaya of the three vajras, he becomes a holder of the vajra of the three bodies;
he shall become an ocean of wish-fulfilling jewels for all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
The one whose nature is vajra illuminates the world-system in every direction;
at the conclusion of the accomplishment of the wheel-samaya, he becomes equal to the Buddha-body.
The perfected one shall wander everywhere, as far as all the sands of the Ganges;
he shall become the lord of the Vidyādharas among all the foremost of commitments.
(From *Sarvasamayasiddhyagradhāraṇī*, p. 57): Through the power of the Body-Vajra, one becomes the sole illuminator of a thousandfold world-system among all forms of invisibility.
He takes away all the accomplishments (siddhis) of the Buddhas and enjoys a maiden born from the foremost of the gods.
With the vajra-eye, one beholds Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding within the abode of the three vajras, as clearly as if they were a single object in one's own hand.
Whatever sounds are proclaimed throughout realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
he hears them from all sides, as if situated within his own ear, by the power of his supernormal knowledge.
He knows the characteristics of the body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings— those which are like the sands of the Ganges— as being the manifestation of a drama called "mind."

One should remember the duration of one's former abodes, which arose during the persistence of cyclic existence for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, just as one recalls the passing of days.
With activities equal in number to the sands of the Ganges, adorned by clouds of Buddhas and the like,
one should emanate [these] for eons equal to the sands of the Ganges, O wielder of the firm and supreme vajra.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Knower of the Samaya: "The adamantine eye, the adamantine ear, the adamantine mind, the adamantine speech,
and the adamantine miraculous power—
through the complete accomplishment of the purpose of the Buddha’s superknowledges, one becomes equal to the body of a Buddha."
Surrounded by a retinue numbering as many as the sands of the Ganges,
he who possesses the vajra of body and speech shall traverse all world-systems in every direction.
The union of the time of service, arising from the secondary means (upasādhana),
the time of the means for the purpose [of attainment], and the fourth, the great means (mahāsādhana).
Having understood this through the Vajrabheda [tantra], one should then accomplish the ritual activities;
one should cultivate the union of service and meditative absorption for the sake of supreme enlightenment.
In the culmination of the *upasādhana* accomplishment, there is the investigation of the vajra-bases;
in the *sādhana*, the exhortation is proclaimed as the meditation on the Lord of Mantras.
At the times of the great accomplishment, having meditated on the Lord as the crown ornament upon the image of one's own Mantra-Vajrin, one attains the accomplishment of the Knowledge-Vajrin.
One should always and in every way perform [the practice] with the nectar of service and knowledge;
for this is the accomplisher of the purpose of all mantras among all mantras.
In great forest regions, in solitary places,
and in vast mountain caves, accomplishment is always attained.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāsādhanavajra.
Now, the service (*sevā*) should be performed with the four vajras by those firm in their vows.
Meditating with the mantra of the three vajra-bodies, one attains accomplishment.
Through the practice of the four junctions at the five locations, the wise one,
having meditated with the wisdom-vajra of the syllable Oṃ, shall enter the *saṃvara*.
Within seven days, a fortnight, a month, or even a year,
having generated the vajra-samaya, accomplishment is swiftly attained.
I have explained this in detail according to the distinctions of the days; within the span of a fortnight, success is declared by those born of the foremost secrets.
In this regard, the following concerns the commitment (*samvara*) of the subsidiary means (*upasādhana*):
The glorious one, who bears the Buddha-body, is cultivated through the indivisibility of the three vajras.
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who are meditated upon as inseparable from the three vajras, grant me today the state of empowerment of the Body-Vajra. (This verse is repeated in C.)
May they today perform for me the rite of empowerment, characterized by the body.
In this regard, the following concerns the subject matter of the *sādhana-saṃvara*.
May the glorious Dharma, the path of speech, cultivated as the indivisibility of the three vajras,
grant me today the state of empowerment for the Vajra of Speech.
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who are realized as the indivisibility of the three vajras,
grant him the state of empowerment arising from the path of speech.
In this regard,
this is the domain of the great accomplishment vow (*mahāsādhanasambara*):
"The glorious Holder of the Mind-Vajra is meditated upon as the indivisibility of the three vajras."
May those who possess the vajra-mind grant me the state of empowerment this very day.
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who are conceived as the indivisibility of the three vajras and who arise from the mind, grant me the state of empowerment today.
Whether it be the Buddha, Vajradharma, or even Vajrasattva—if one who is deluded in nature should transgress [this command], they will surely burst apart; of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter, the instruction on the foremost means of achieving the commitments (*samayasādhanāgranirdeśa*), in the *Śrī-guhyasamāja*, the great king of secret tantras, the most secret of secrets concerning the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
The Thirteenth Chapter.

Now, the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas who move at the pinnacle of the wisdom-vajra, and the wise Bodhisattvas who have arisen for the sake of all sentient beings—[kh, g: the enjoyments; k: from the left].
Having prostrated before the Great Teacher, the Sage who holds the vajra for the sake of sentient beings and who knows the reality of the pledge of worship, he uttered this sound of the vajra:
"Aho! The divine method of the Buddha! Aho! The supreme method of awakening!"
Oh, how peaceful is the way of Dharma! Oh, how firm is the way of Mantra!
When phenomena have not arisen and possess no excellence of intrinsic nature,
the arising of non-conceptual knowledge regarding those phenomena is proclaimed.
Speak, O Blessed One, the delightful *Sarvadharmasamuccaya*,
the great wisdom of vajra-recitation, the maṇḍala inseparable from the three bodies.
The wisdoms of the Buddhas are attained through the meditations on the indivisibility of the three vajras;
by reciting with the application of the vajra, one is empowered by all the Buddhas.

The characteristic of the body, speech, and mind of all the families and all mantras is the recitation of mantras; having proclaimed it aloud, he then uttered the vajra-recitation: "Listen, O oceans of gnosis!"
And the Buddhas, arisen throughout the three times, who possess the vajras of body, speech, and mind, have attained incomparable gnosis through the cultivation of vajra mantras. Thus it is said.
Then the Teacher Vajradhara, born from the wisdom of the space-vajra,
the agent and creator, the most excellent and supreme among the best, proclaimed the vajra-recitation.

In the recitation of the meaning of all mantras, this placement (*nyāsa*)—which has the characteristic of the indivisibility of the three vajras and culminates in the vajra at the three divisions—is called the "three vajras."
And so it is said:
"A threefold vibration should be performed in the presence of body, speech, and mind;
by means of this vajra-recitation, one becomes equal to the Vajra-mind."

Having meditated upon the body, speech, and mind of the Buddhas, the arrangement of worship should be performed by the Wisdom-Vajra; this brings about the attainment of enlightenment. It is equal to the mind of the Three Vajras.
[It] would be.
Alternatively, one should perform the vibration individually according to the three divisions;
one should cause the selflessness of body, speech, and mind to vibrate thoroughly by means of the gnosis-mind.
While reciting it, one should emanate the vajra; at the conclusion, one should indicate its withdrawal.
This is the [practice] of all Buddhas whose eyes are opened by primordial wisdom.
The realization of the body-vajra, which is the investigation of existence and non-existence, is proclaimed as the "Buddha-body"; that is called the recitation of the body.
The thorough realization of the convention of speech, and the investigation of words and non-words—this is declared to be the Vajra of Speech; it is called the recitation of speech.
The perfect awakening to the commitment of the mind, the investigation of the vajra of stability—
this is called the vajra-mind, and it is termed the mental recitation.
Then, through the recitation that follows [the mantra], which is beautiful and devoid of intrinsic nature,
the investigation of the Buddhas of the three times is called the "jewel-recitation."
The emanation of a body-cloud from the Buddha-field in all directions for the sake of the vajra-gone-and-returning is called the unfailing recitation.

62) One hears the syllables and words of the mantra resounded by one's own vajras throughout the maṇḍala;
that is called the recitation of the wrathful deity through the wisdom of the wrathful samaya.

Having perceived those who are distracted by the objects of desire and who seek neither protection nor welfare anywhere, one establishes them in the state of delusion; this is known as the "recitation of delusion."
The speech arising from Rāgavajra, which is established in body, speech, and mind,
places all sentient beings in the state of passion; this is known as the recitation born of passion (rāgajāpa).
The mind arising from the vajra of hatred is established in body, speech, and mind;
having established sentient beings in the abode of hatred, that is called the recitation of hatred.
The reality of the three-vajra commitment is the central Samayavajrin;
that very state is called the neuter recitation of all vajras.
All the Vajra Lords, who contemplate the meaning of the reality of passion,
bring about the awakening born of passion, which seeks the welfare of all sentient beings.
The great vidyās, Locanā and the others, who are eternally intent upon the purpose of desire,
are accomplished through the enjoyment of desires when they are served according to one's wish.
The Vidyārājas, the Vajrins born from the pledge of delusion (mohasamaya),
who have attained accomplishment in the state of the neuter, bestow supreme accomplishment.
Born from anger and the abode of hatred, they are constantly intent on killing;
through the purpose of killing, they achieve success when served according to one's desire.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Being’s Commitment (Mahāpuruṣasamaya):
“One should meditate on the wheel situated in the center of the heart of those who possess the vajra of gnosis.”
The meditation on the meaning of the wheel-mantra situated in the center of the pure maṇḍala [is the meaning of the central wheel].
One should meditate on the vajra [or wheel] situated in the center of the heart of the Wisdom-Vajra-holder;
this is the meditation on the meaning of the vajra-mantra, located in the center of the vajra-maṇḍala.
One who possesses the wisdom of the Jewel should meditate on the jewel situated in the center of the heart;
this is the meditation on the meaning of the Jewel mantra, located in the middle of the Jewel maṇḍala.
The knower of the lotus should meditate on a lotus situated in the center of the heart;
this is the meditation on the meaning of the lotus mantra, located in the center of the Dharma-maṇḍala.
The knower of the sword-mantra should meditate on a sword situated in the center of the heart;
this is the meditation on the meaning of the sword-mantra, located within the center of the pledge-maṇḍala.
One should establish all the Buddhas on all sides of the maṇḍala;
by radiating them forth through the differentiation of five rays,
one attains awakening.
The emanation of all mantras is proclaimed to be twofold;
through the division of the three vajra-bodies, there occurs the emanation and reabsorption.
By worshipping the body with its own nature, the mind with the nature of the mind, and speech with the nature of speech, one shall obtain the fruit of worship.
Through the great maṇḍala wheel, one performs the visualization of the five vajras;
having meditated on the Lord in the center as one's own form, the possessor of the three kāya-vajras.
Having visualized the fourfold mandalas of one's own mantra-vajra according to the four colors, one should cultivate the meditation on the meaning of the mantra within the heart.
This fourfold vajra performs the activity of the Dhyānavajrin;
for this is the supreme, eternal secret of all mantras.
