In rites of pacification (śāntika), one should take the form of Locanā; in rites of enrichment (pauṣṭika), the form of Padmavajrī; in rites of subjugation (vaśya), the state of Vairocana; and in rites of malevolent magic (abhicāraka), the form of Vajrakrodha.
This is that secret of all mantras, born from the three bodies;
it was fashioned by the Wisdom-Vajra and is characterized by the drama of ritual action.
This rite of incitement should be performed against beings who speak words of non-devotion, those who revile the Teacher or the Vajrī,
and other such wicked persons.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahājñānacakravajra:
"One should visualize all those residing in the three realms within the Buddha-body (*buddhakāya*),
having rendered them as joined together and then opened wide."
Then follows the establishment of karma.
One should visualize Vajrasattva, who is situated in the center of the element of space, possessing a five-pronged vajra and four faces, and endowed with the excellence of all aspects.
One should visualize the Buddha-wheel, which has arisen from the samaya of the three times;
this Buddha-wheel of great power is to be formed upon the right hand.
Having gathered together all sentient beings born in the ten directions through the differentiation of the Buddha-body,
one should cause them to enter one's own body by means of the yoga of the mass.
Furthermore, the emanation of the Buddhas who possess the vajra of gnosis should be performed by visualizing them as wrathful,
agitated by rage, and terrifyingly fierce and formidable.
With the tips of their hands grasping various weapons, and intent upon the supreme purpose of killing,
they slay even the most wicked beings— and Vajrasattva himself.
The Buddhas, bestowers of the boon of the three bodies within the maṇḍala that is the abode of the three vajras, grant accomplishment; one whose nature is deluded dies—of this there is no doubt.
This task is not accomplished even by a Buddha in seven days.
(pdf 57, p.
65) This is the samādhi called the Vajra-Samaya-Command-Wheel.
One should visualize Vairocana, situated in the center of the space-element wheel, adorned with vajra-flames and endowed with the excellence of all aspects.
One should visualize in his hand a vajra dense with sparks, representing the great sacrificial offerings— the Vajrasattvas born from the samaya of the three times.

Having gathered together the sentient beings arisen in the ten directions through the differentiation of the vajra-body by means of the yoga of light rays, one should cause them to enter into one's own body.
The vibration of all vajras is to be performed by one of supreme wisdom;
let all those whose nature is that of the Buddhas, who are united with body, speech, and mind, listen!
I am the glorious Vajradhara; through the differentiation of the wheel of command, I emanate those born of the three bodies by means of the blazing vajra-form.
If one should transgress the commitment, it will undoubtedly fall apart.
This is the samādhi called "The Vajra of the Command of the Wheel Commitment."
One should contemplate the Vajra-holder of the Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
one should visualize Yamāntaka as the great wheel known as the space-vajra.
And having caused the Buddhas born in the three times to enter the maṇḍala of the three bodies,
one should again emanate the Buddhas appearing in the form of Yamāntaka.
And one should visualize, while enraged, that all beings born in the three times who are enemies with malicious minds have been slain; this is the Vajra Command Maṇḍala.
The samādhi named "The Vajra of the Command of the Three Bodies, Equal to Yamāntaka, Arising from All Samayas."
(From *pdf* 58, p.
66) By means of the vajras of body, speech, and mind, or by the quality of the meaning of one’s own mantra,
or else at the time of the flower-offering (*pauṣpa*), the turning of the wheel of command (*ājñācakra*) is performed.
[The purpose] ||
For the sake of protecting all mantras, this must be performed by those who possess the supreme vajra of wisdom;
this is declared for the purpose of protecting the enlightenment of all Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Bodhicitta:
"Having meditated upon the Dharma situated in the center of the space-vajra, which arises from the supreme Vairocana,
one should arrange the seat that is the foremost of the vajras of the three bodies."
One should visualize the entire realm of space as completely filled with all the Buddhas;
one should conceive the gnosis of the mantra-syllables and phrases as the very form of the mind.
Furthermore, one should again manifest the Buddhas produced from the mind-vajra;
having identified them as the mind-vajra, one should cause them to enter into the three bodies.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra-Samaya of Space. This is the samādhi called "The Illuminator of the Jewel of Vajra Mantras."
One should visualize the Vajrasattva endowed with the excellence of all aspects;
having sequentially established the Buddhas, one should walk upon the water. By means of the application of the pledge-water, one visualizes the placement of one's feet upon the head [of the beings].
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Pure by Nature. This is the samādhi called "Treading upon the Vajra-Ocean."
Having meditated upon the Maheśvara maṇḍala, one should place the Family of Wrath in its center;
one should visualize him with his head trampled by Karmavajra.
And so it is said: "The samādhi named 'Vajra that Stuns All Heretics and Proponents of Other Schools'."
(From *pdf* 58, p.

67) Having visualized all [the deities] in a wrathful form, with the tips of their three vajras resembling yellow filaments, one should contemplate them as being like the king of mountains and manifest them upon the crown of the head.
Even the army of the Buddhas perishes when struck by the pillar; of this there is no doubt.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, who has arisen from the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas. This is the samādhi named "Paralyzer of All Armies."
At the time of terrifying the enemies, one should perform this meditation;
if a Buddha should transgress it, he would burst apart—of this there is no doubt.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Trivajrasamaya:
"Having meditated upon the *hūṃ*-syllable as a stake (*kīlaka*) with the proportions of a five-pronged [vajra], one has thereby fashioned the vajra-stake; one should visualize that within the heart."
Even the army of the Buddhas, if enraged, would go to destruction; of this there is no doubt.
The meditative absorption named "The Great Destroyer of Enemies" (or "The Destroyer of Delusion").
Whether in a city, a village, or a district, one should employ this;
by this, there shall always be peace, free from all diseases.
One should visualize a five-pronged vajra situated in the intermediate space;
having meditated upon it as being like the conflagration at the end of an eon, one should then command its withdrawal.
Furthermore, one should perform a vibration with the radiance of jewels and wish-fulfilling gems;
one should indeed meditate upon the clouds of Dharma and bestow the consecration.
By means of this vajra of meditative concentration, even that which is difficult to fill becomes completely filled;
he shall become the glorious wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi), the accomplisher of the vajra of giving.
It should be pervaded by clouds of Buddhas, the great Dharmas, and Vajrasattvas.
(pdf 59, p.
68) That which abides for three incalculable eons is empowered by all the Buddhas.
This is that untainted secret of the body of all the Buddhas.
The samādhi named "The Arising of the Vajra that Removes the Illnesses of All Sentient Beings."
Wherever one should practice the undertaking with the vajra of meditation,
by abiding in this yoga of meditation, one is empowered by the Buddhas.
One should visualize the great king Dhvajāmṛta as a vajra-stake,
blazing like sparks of fire, and drive it into the circle of the ten directions.
And so it is said: "The samādhi named Jagadvijayaśāntivajra."
One should contemplate the supreme peace maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-element;
having meditated upon the form of Vairocana, one should then place it within the heart.
One should visualize the element of space completely filled with the foremost Locanās;
then, having withdrawn them into a mass of light rays, one should cast it down upon the beginning.
The practitioner, becoming wise, should radiate clouds of Buddhas through the openings at the tips of his pores;
then indeed, those clouds of Buddhas bestow empowerment upon him,
and by this, he becomes the glorious Vajrasamaya in that very instant.
The Samādhi called the Array of Clouds of the Buddha-Samaya.
One should contemplate the auspicious Maheśvara-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having meditated upon the image as the supreme Dharma, one should then place it within the heart.
One should fill the delightful realm of the space-element with those known as Pāṇḍara;
one should then withdraw it by means of a mass of rays,
possessing the luster of a precious wish-fulfilling jewel.
To one who requests it at the abode of body, speech, and mind, the practitioner should offer that [teaching];
the observer of vows should emit clouds of jewels from the openings at the tips of the pores of the skin.
One should meditate upon the Cloud of Dharma and bestow the consecration.
By means of this vajra of meditation, even that which is difficult to fill becomes completely filled;
he becomes the glorious wish-fulfilling gem, the accomplisher of the vajra of giving.
The Samādhi called the Array of Clouds of the Dharma Commitment.
One should contemplate the mandala of the Vajra-Moon-Jewel situated in the center of the space-element;
one who desires [attainment] should place the image of the supreme Dharma of Space-Vajra within the heart.
The circle of space is completely filled with Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
by means of the application of five-colored rays, one should cause splendor to descend there.
At that very moment, he would become pleasing to all the Buddhas;
resembling Mañjuśrī himself, he would become a performer of the deeds of others.
And with a joyful heart and great enthusiasm, he bestows consecration;
he brings all people under his control merely by being seen, as they are impelled [by him].
The Samādhi called the Array of Jewel Clouds of Commitment.
One should visualize the space-vajra [as filled] with cruel and fierce rākṣasas, extremely terrible in their wrath,
as well as various jackals, crows, vultures, and dogs.
One should always visualize the enemies as being situated within a fiery maṇḍala; having meditated thus upon one who harms all the Buddhas, one should apply the yoga.
One should visualize all the entrails, marrow, blood, and so forth being drawn out;
the enemy, overwhelmed by those bearing various weapons, shall die.
(From PDF 60, p.
70) If by this [practice] one is empowered as either a Buddha or a Vajradhara within the completion of half a month, one will die; of this there is no doubt.
The meditative absorption named "The Array of the Vajra Cloud Samaya."
One should visualize Vairocana with three faces, possessing a radiance like the stalk of an autumn lotus,
white, black, and deep red, adorned with a crown of matted hair.
One should visualize the three-faced Vajrin, with faces that are black, red, and white;
he wears a crown of matted hair, is blazing, and pervades the entire world-system.
One should contemplate the three-faced one who possesses passion, with faces red, black, and white;
by meditating upon him as adorned with a crown of matted locks, one certainly attains success.
One should visualize a wheel, a vajra, and a great lotus in the right hands;
one should visualize the six arms as holding vajras and various auspicious weapons.
One should contemplate Locanā, who desires the welfare of all beings; she has three faces—white, black, and deep red—and one should visualize her as having a beautiful form.
One should always meditate upon the Great Queen Khavajranetrī, who has three faces;
one should visualize her as having a beautiful form, with faces that are black, red, and white.
One should always meditate upon Vāgvajrī, the Great Queen, who has three faces;
one should visualize her as having a beautiful complexion, appearing red, white, and black.
The Vidyā holds a vajra and an utpala, has three faces, and possesses a beautiful, radiant luster.
By meditating on him as having yellow, black, and white forms, one shall attain gnosis—
the great wrathful Yamāntaka, who has three faces and a radiant, furious splendor.
One should visualize the fierce fear of even fear itself as being black in color—
the invincible Great Wrathful One, who utters a loud, boisterous laugh.
One should contemplate [the deity] as having three faces, dense with sparks, and radiating light.

One should always meditate through yoga upon Hayagrīva, the great wrathful one, who arises like the conflagration at the end of an aeon, possessing three faces and treading upon the wicked with his feet.
Vajrāmṛta, the great wrathful one, whose mind is filled with sparks of fire,
resembling a blazing vajra, cruel, and the source of fear even for fear itself.
One should visualize the great wrathful Ṭakkirāja, who has three faces that bestow the three fears, four arms, and is the foremost among those who inspire dread.

One should always meditate upon the three-faced one, who possesses great strength and the great vajra, who sustains the purpose of the meaning of the three worlds, and who is the destroyer of all malevolent beings.
[Vajrāmṛta and Ṭakkirāja follow this line.]
One should visualize the great wrathful Nīladaṇḍa, who instills fear in the three worlds,
possessing three faces, arisen from the three vajras, and emitting sharp flames.
The practitioner should meditate upon the great wrathful Vajrācala, squint-eyed and born of the vajra; he is gentle, possesses three faces, and holds a sword and a noose.
One should meditate upon the blazing three-faced Vajrin within the mandala of meditation, who is the single-syllabled Mahoṣṇīṣa radiating light in all directions.
One should meditate upon Sumbha, the bearer of the supreme gnosis, who is fierce and possesses a radiance like an ocean of fear;
he has three faces, a body of blazing flames, and is brilliantly radiant through meditation.
The Tejorāśi-jayoṣṇīṣa and those others who are Vajra-holders of mantra—
these should each be meditated upon through these enjoyments of the samaya.
Innumerable meditative absorptions (*samādhi*) have been proclaimed for the mantras;
however, each individual wrathful deity (*krodha*) is distinguished by its great multiplicity.
One should contemplate the supreme, translucent maṇḍala situated in the center of the element of space;
having manifested the form of a Buddha, one should manifest Vairocana.

One should contemplate the supreme wheel-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should visualize Locanā, the foremost of goddesses.
She has a beautiful face and large eyes, adorned with various ornaments,
complete with all the auspicious marks, and the bearer of the foremost of the three bodies. [Having manifested the image of the Buddha, one should manifest the supreme Khavajrā.]
One should visualize the wheel in one's hand, which brings the three realms under control;
it is the wisdom that accomplishes all siddhis and bestows the wish-fulfilling jewel.
The samādhi called "Possessing the Foremost Hand of the Wisdom of Locanā’s Samaya."
One should contemplate the supreme moon-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra.
Having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest Khavajrāgrī,
who has a beautiful face, wide eyes, and a luster like that of a blue lotus.
One should visualize one's own supreme consort, complete with all the primary marks,
holding in her hand a blue lotus and a wheel that is honored by the three realms.
This divine secret that brings about the awakening of the Buddhas for the Vajra-holders who have attained siddhi is called the Samādhi of the Delightful Vajra Clouds of Sunbeams Pervading Space.
One should contemplate the supreme Dharma-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the image of the Buddha, one should manifest Dharmavajrī.
She has a beautiful face and large eyes, resembling the finest ruby;
she is born from the tip of the net of illusion, and is most dear to him who is colored by passion.

Perfectly endowed with all the [major] marks and adorned with all ornaments, she holds in her hand a divine red lotus empowered by all the Buddhas.
The divine, secret source of the knowledge of phenomena for those who hold the vajra of the samaya;
this is the samādhi called "the vajra that reveals the perfect awakening to the reality of the dharma-samaya."
One should contemplate the supreme maṇḍala of accomplishment situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should then manifest Tārā as the foremost.
Having meditated upon her who has a beautiful face and large eyes, adorned with various ornaments,
resembling the color of gold, and eager for the passion of women's guile— [this is the triple object of accomplishment].
One should clearly manifest in one’s hand a blue lotus resembling yellow [in hue],
born from the vajra-samādhi and honored by all sentient beings.
The Samādhi called the Supreme Samayatārā.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should visualize the foremost Yamāntaka.
One should visualize the circle of Bhava as blazing with a dense mass of sparks, wrathful,
red-eyed, with terrifying fangs, and holding a sword in his hand.
Having meditated on the station of Vairocana upon the crown, the Vajra-holders are pleased;
for this is the commitment (*samaya*) of all the Wrathful Ones who possess the Vajra of Gnosis.
The samādhi called the Array of the Radiant Manifestation of Yamāntaka’s Pulsation.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of a Buddha, one should manifest the one known as Aparājita.
One should visualize him as white in color, blazing with a dense mass of sparks, his waist girdled by serpents,
and possessing a terrifying, wide-open mouth.

For this is the commitment of all the Wrathful Ones who possess the Vajra of Gnosis.
The samādhi called the Invincible Vajra Array.
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of a Buddha, one should manifest Hayagrīva.
One should visualize [the deity] as red in color, filled with sparks, wrathful, flashing forth on all sides, and treading upon all wicked beings.
Having meditated on the Buddha Amitābha upon the crown, the Vajra-holders are satisfied;
for this is the pledge (samaya) of all the Wrathful Ones who possess the Vajra of Gnosis.

One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest Vajrāmṛta.
One should visualize [him] as dense with sparks, blazing, filled with clouds of thunderbolts,
wrathful, full of rage, black, and possessing sharp fangs.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, the wrathful deity is pleased;
for this is the samaya of all wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress.

One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having visualized the form of a Buddha, one should manifest the being Ṭakkirāja.
One should visualize [the deity] as fierce, with disheveled hair-tips, terrifying even to fear itself,
adorned with all ornaments, and possessing the brilliant luster of a vajra.

One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should manifest the Great Power.
One should meditate upon the powerful Vajrin, who is fierce, wrathful, and holds a noose; he is a blazing maṇḍala, the abode of the three vajras, dense with sparks.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction,
this indeed is the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress.

One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;

and is blazing and dense with sparks.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction (or nourishment),
this indeed is the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress.

One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having manifested the form of the Buddha, one should visualize the summit of Acala.
One should visualize the immovable Vajrin as squint-eyed, deformed, and wrathful, holding a noose and a sword, agitated, blazing with a dense mass of sparks, and radiant.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction, this is indeed the samaya of all the wrathful deities, difficult to transgress. (pdf 63, p. 77)

One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;

One should visualize the Uṣṇīṣacakrasamaya, complete with all the marks, surrounded by a blazing wheel, and radiating light.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction,
this indeed is the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress.
The Samādhi called the Uṣṇīṣa-Vidyācala-Cakra (the Wheel of the Mountain of the Uṣṇīṣa Knowledge), [also known as the Holder of the Samaya].
One should contemplate the supreme solar mandala situated in the center of the space-vajra;
having visualized the form of the Buddha, one should manifest Vajrasumbha.
By meditating upon him whose body consists of sharp, blazing rays, who is like a thunderbolt-bearing cloud,
holding a vajra in his hand, and possessing great flames, one shall attain accomplishment.
Having meditated upon the Akṣobhya-samaya in the crown, which increases satisfaction,
this indeed is the samaya of all the wrathful deities, which is difficult to transgress.

Through the wheel of the cessation of anger, which serves the wheel of the Buddhas,
the concentrations and vajra-knowledges are accomplished from the vajra-maṇḍala.

Then, as soon as this song was sung, all those wise ones who possess every perfection were satisfied and attained great joy, recollecting the Buddha-vajra.

In the dwelling: perform, perform all rites;
cut, cut all mantras; pierce, pierce the supreme mudrās; summon, summon all spirits;

Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Do not delay, do not delay!
Remember your pledge! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ! Shatter, shatter! O fulfiller of all hopes, destroy all enemies! Act, act! O Blessed One, why do you tarry?
Accomplish, accomplish all my aims, svāhā!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the Buddhas of great renown became afraid, their minds filled with terror, as they recollected the Vajra-mind.
Having obtained a skull-bowl that is free of cracks and possesses a beautiful form,

Having recited the names of Locanā and Māmakī, who belong to the great Vajra family,

Then, as soon as this was sung, all the Buddhas of great renown became afraid, their minds filled with terror, and they recollected the thought of awakening (bodhicitta).

Arising by their very own nature, they move throughout the three realms;
one who desires the welfare of all sentient beings should practice the entire samaya.
The samādhi named "The Convergence of the Samaya of All the Three Realms" [and the Vajra].
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, brought forth from the vajras of body, speech, and mind the Vajra of the Samaya of Body-Accomplishment.
One should always cause all three types of physical [actions] arising from the Vajra to perform the Buddha-activities for the realm of sentient beings everywhere. (pdf 90, p. 131)
Then Vajrapāṇi, the sovereign of all Tathāgatas, brought forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the Vajra of the Samaya of Speech-Siddhi.
The entire stainless mandala of the three worlds is produced by the action of speech;
this commitment (*samaya*), delightful as the state of perfection in speech, is difficult to transgress.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the lord of all Tathāgatas, brought forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the Vajra-samaya of the accomplishment of the mind.
One who holds the firm vajra should visualize everything as consisting of the mind-vajra;
for this is declared to be the commitment (samaya) of those who possess the indestructible vajra of the three vajras.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Samantabhadra, Vajrasattva, who is beautiful with mantras.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, brought forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the commitment (*samaya*) which is the essence of all mantra-vajras.
By paying homage through the union of body, speech, and mind to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise Śrāvakas, one shall attain non-perishing.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the lord of all Tathāgatas, brought forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the samaya of the vajra-meditation of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
In all cases within the maṇḍala of the body, speech, and mind of Vajrasattva,
the practitioner of mantra recitation should perform meditation through the yoga of the three vajras.
Then Vajrapāṇi,
the Lord of all Tathāgatas, [expounded] the *samaya* of the commitment (*samvara*) for the accomplishment of all mantra-vajras.
He caused [it] to issue forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.
One should briefly impel the realm of sentient beings with the vajra of meditative concentration;
this is the vow arising from the vajra, the most supreme among the foremost salutations of the three vajras.

Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, brought forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the commitment-restraint (*samaya-saṃvara*) of the service, accomplishment, near-accomplishment, and great accomplishment.
One should contemplate the element of space as completely filled with the vajra of feces and urine;
one should offer this to the Buddhas of the three times—this is the supreme, eternal samaya.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, brought forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the samaya of the disappearance of all vajras.

The Vajra-holder should desire [the consort] every day at the four junctions of the day according to the best method. He should also constantly offer the ritual substance; this is the commitment that fulfills the vajra.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, brought forth the Samaya of the Sky-Vidyādharas from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.
One should contemplate the meditation upon the crowns of the vajras of body, speech, and mind;
it cannot be conquered by any of the wrathful ones through the samayas of the three vajras.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, brought forth from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind the samaya of the beginner practitioners who uphold all mantras.
In the vessel of the body-vajra and of the external Vajradhara,
the ritual action for opening the sutras should always be performed by means of the vajra-phenomena.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra of Innate Purity.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas...
Having contemplated the equality of the vajra-heart of the body, speech, and mind of all Vajradharas, he became silent.

Then indeed, bodhisattva mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in the Sumeru mountains of unspeakably unspeakable buddha-fields, having prostrated to all the Tathāgatas, spoke thus: "Why does this Blessed One,
Vajradhara, the sovereign of all Tathāgatas, [remain] in the midst of the maṇḍala assembly of all the Tathāgatas and bodhisattvas?"
He consented by remaining silent.
Then the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, spoke thus to all those Bodhisattvas:
"O sons of noble family, this syllable-phrase is the nature of the non-apprehensibility of the vajras of body, speech, and mind."
The Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, having contemplated the syllable-word that is devoid of intrinsic nature, remained silent.
And by the thought of this Lord of all Tathāgatas, O sons of good family, this came to pass.
"The body is the unarisen syllable, characterized by the words of speech and mind; it is the space-vajra, arisen from conceptualization, the gathering of false aggregations. Thus [it is said].

Then the great bodhisattvas, headed by Mañjuśrī, spoke thus to all those Tathāgatas: "O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, do not conceptualize the word of the Vajra of Speech through false origination. For what reason?
Because this [Vajra of Speech] follows the course of conduct within the vajra-realms of all Tathāgatas."
[He is] the Lord of the Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas. For what reason?

There are great Bodhisattvas, such as Brahmā and others, who have attained the knowledge of the great superknowledges (*mahābhijñā*), yet, not knowing the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the characteristics of all phenomena, they conceptualize thus: "What is this?"
Without realizing the reality of the Dharma-vajra of all Tathāgatas, he teaches the secret syllable as the great vajra-self of all Tathāgatas (pdf 92,

Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas said this to those Bodhisattvas: "Wait a moment, O Great Bodhisattvas! Even we, having attained the secret syllable of the vajra body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, do not know the awakening of body, speech, and mind. For what reason? Because it is produced from the syllable that is devoid of intrinsic nature."

Regarding the adamantine perfect awakening of non-arising: O sons of noble family, as many sentient beings as there are who are included within the gathering of sentient beings, they are all established in awakening; they are the Buddhas of the Vajra. Why is that?
Because, indeed, these sentient beings have attained the wisdom of the vajra of body, speech, and mind, by virtue of the reality-nature (*dharmatā*) of the three bodies of the Vajra.
[The word *varaṇā*]; then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, spoke thus to those Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas:
In the self-nature pure and devoid of self, in the dharmadhātu free from abiding,
conceptualization born of the vajra is both proclaimed and not proclaimed.

Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having paid homage to the Blessed Mahāvajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, spoke thus: "Blessed One, from where do these vajra-attainments of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas emerge, and wherein are they established?"
Vajradhara, the sovereign of all Tathāgatas, said:

"O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, you are established in the vajra-continuum of the equality of your own body, speech, and mind; [you are] all accomplishments, all vajra-knowledges, and everything up to the triple world."

All the Tathāgatas said: "O Blessed One, where do the vajra-attainments of the body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas, as well as the entire triple world, abide? The Lord of the Wisdom of All the Tathāgatas replied:
(From *pdf* 92, p. 135):

"O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, the vajra-attainments of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, as well as the entire triple world, are established in the element of space. Thus spoke all the Tathāgatas.
“Blessed One, where does space abide? Vajradhara replied, “Nowhere.
Then all those Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, having attained a state of wonder and amazement, [said] this:
They raised a cry of Dharma:
"O Vajra! O Vajra! O teaching of the Vajra!
Where there is no body, speech, or mind, there form is manifested."
Then the Teacher Vajradhara, who is honored by all Buddhas,
the foremost of the three vajras, the most eminent of the great, the triple-vajra Supreme Lord—
He speaks of the meditation on the Vidyāpuruṣa for the sake of all accomplishments:
one should meditate upon the Buddha-maṇḍala situated in the center of the space-vajra-realm.
Having manifested the body-vajra, one should manifest the vajra at the crown of the head;
one should contemplate it as having three faces, arisen from the three bodies, and radiating light.
Having meditated upon the Holder of the Vajra-Wheel, one shall swiftly attain enlightenment.
According to the distinctions of the families, one should contemplate this secret for all;
otherwise, their meditation will not result in supreme accomplishment.
And thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vidyāpuruṣa-Vajraguhya.
One should visualize the Great Queen, who has become the very elements, as she brings satisfaction;
in this way, those Bull-like Ones, whose vajra-bodies possess the three characteristics, are pleased.
Any highly renowned Bodhisattva of great splendor who should meditate upon this will attain the accomplishment of the three bodies within seven days.
(From PDF 93, p.

136) Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, once again brought forth from his own body, speech, and mind-vajras the secret mystery of the compendium of body, speech, and mind-vajras.

One should meditate according to the ritual procedure upon all the commitments of body, speech, and mind, which are the conceptualization of the meaning of Mahāmudrā; in an instant, one shall attain Buddhahood.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, once again brought forth [this teaching] from the vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all practitioners:
"If one desires supreme accomplishment (or enlightenment), one should not bind hand-mudrās."
This is the commitment of all mantras, which cannot be transgressed even by the Victors.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the lord of all Tathāgatas, once again brought forth the samaya of all Buddhas from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.
One should never feel disgust for feces, urine, semen, and blood;
one should always consume this secret born of the three vajras according to the prescribed rite.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the lord of all Tathāgatas, once again issued forth the speech-vajra commitment from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.
Whatever women are known to exist on the delightful paths of the three realms, one may desire them all according to the ritual; by means of the vajras of speech, one is not to be censured.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the sovereign of all Tathāgatas, once again brought forth the Mind-Vajra Samaya from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.
As many as all the pledges (samaya) residing within the body of the three vajras, they satisfy the mind-vajra through the vajra-pledges; one should not feel revulsion toward them.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Trivajrasamaya [Kh: adds *vajraḥ*]. Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, once again [emanated] the Secret-Vajra of all Tathāgatas from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind.
He uttered this:
"The five aggregates have been proclaimed by the Muni as the five Buddhas;
the vajras are the sense bases themselves, the maṇḍala of the foremost Bodhisattvas."
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, again brought forth the Samuccayavajra of the three realms from the vajras of his own body, speech, and mind:
"Earth is known as Locanā; the element of water is remembered as Māmakī."
The fire element is called Pāṇḍarā; wind is proclaimed to be Tārā.
She herself is the commitment of the space-vajra element, and is remembered as Vajradhara.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Lord of the realms of all Tathāgatas, the Great Vajrasattva. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajra of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, entered the meditative absorption named "Abiding in the Equality of All Tathāgatas. Having entered that state, he surveyed the entire mandala of the assembly of all Tathāgatas.
He remained silent. Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, having prostrated before all the Tathāgatas, spoke thus:
"I have been consecrated into the secret assembly of the vajra body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas... [k: adds *rahasyam*; kh:]

"How should the Blessed One, the Vajrācārya, be viewed by all the Tathāgatas and all the Bodhisattvas?
